verdict.rationale: Graphite's docs describe its AI code review agent as "codebase-aware", and Graphite Chat on the review page can "find related files, understand dependencies". Together these are first-party claims of context beyond the diff, but there is no detail on how review comments draw on call sites, related modules, or existing conventions. Custom rules let teams state conventions explicitly, but that is user-defined input, not inferred repository understanding. Missing for 10: documentation of how review comments use repo-wide context (call sites, cross-module impact, inferred conventions), any example comments showing whole-repo reasoning, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, review comments reflect the whole repository — call sites, related modules, existing conventions — not just the changed hunks

citations.quote: Get immediate, actionable feedback with Graphite’s codebase-aware AI code review agent.
Find related files, understand dependencies, and get context from other PRs without switching tabs.
AI reviews analyze every pull request in your repositories, identifying potential issues and suggesting fixes instantly
